title: Underlying finite etale extension of a generically split torsor
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated integral normal scheme, $c:C\to S$ a quasi-compact, quasi-separated smooth morphism with geometrically connected fibres, and $\sigma:S\to C$ a section [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $K=\kappa(\eta)$ for the function field of $S$ at its generic point and $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ for the canonical map. Let $q:C_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $j:C_\eta\to C$ make a cartesian square with $i,c$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $s_\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to C_\eta$ satisfy $s_\eta q=1$ and $s_\eta j=i\sigma$. Let $G$ be a finite group with invertible order on $S$, and $Z\to C_\eta$ a finite etale $G$-torsor with a $K$-point over $s_\eta$ [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. There exist a scheme $P$, a finite etale surjective morphism $\pi:P\to C$, and $\psi:Z\to P$ such that the square with top $\psi$, bottom $j$, and sides $Z\to C_\eta,\pi$ is cartesian. No action on $P$ is part of this conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0EYJ; Tag 0EZJ, proof: construction of the underlying finite etale morphism, before adding its group action

proof.text: Descend the family, section, group order, generic torsor and rational point to a normal integral Noetherian base. Keep the comparison maps a, k and chi and the pullback square of generic torsors.
Apply the Noetherian extension theorem to the descended data, obtaining P0, a finite etale morphism pi0, and its cartesian generic comparison psi0.

Set P = P0 times_{C0} C and let pi be its projection to C. Finiteness and etaleness are stable under base change. Paste the generic-cover comparison with the descended extension square, rewrite k j0 = j a, and use the universal property of P to construct psi. Cancel the pullback square defining P on the right to prove that psi and j give the required cartesian square (IsPullback.paste_horiz and of_right').

The smooth geometrically connected family C over the integral connected base S is connected (GeometricallyConnected.connectedSpace). The map from Spec K obtained by composing the rational point z with psi makes P nonempty. The finite etale projection pi has a closed image because it is finite and an open image because it is flat and locally of finite presentation. A nonempty clopen subset of a connected space is the entire space (IsClopen.eq_univ). Hence pi is surjective, giving all four clauses of the original conclusion.

proof_origin.note: The Lean proof assembles Noetherian approximation and the Noetherian extension, and proves the pullback comparison and surjectivity directly from Mathlib. The unit route is retained.
